decisions.text: ADOPT run #7's spec rather than author a new one. Run #7 stress-tested and taste-gated an identical trickle brief, reshaped it from guard-accretion to guard-REDUCTION, then delivered zero work cycles (381/381 spawns dead on HTTP 429). Re-authoring the scope would re-derive a conclusion already reached and paid for; L-045 forbids exactly that. Inherited items are re-verified against the repo before prioritization, which already caught one false premise (see D-R8-2).

Run #7's R-1 named a ">= 121 tests" COUNT floor to retire. Cycle 0 grepped test/ at HEAD and found no such literal floor anywhere. The inherited premise is unconfirmed, so S-1 was re-shaped to MEASURE the inventory of count-claim guards first and retire only what the inventory shows exists. L-045 (re-verify inherited SPEC items) and L-031 (measure before planning against an inferred gap) both applied, and both paid at cycle 0.

Taste judge scored use-twice 4 / product-not-demo 6 / scope-fits-night 7 / one-memorable-thing 6 and caught that S-1/S-4/S-5 could each be discharged by publishing prose. Spec CHANGED at lock rather than annotated: S-6 now requires every published finding to ship as a rerunnable tool in tools/, and S-7 requires the escalation to be written as launch-ready brief text for run #9. The use-twice 4 is recorded and not argued away — it is the honest cost of a fourth consecutive trickle brief on a finished program.

L-038 exhausted-window refusal test RUN, not assumed — this is the check the last two runs failed. Probe at kickoff: weekly_used_pct 6.0 at week_elapsed_pct 4.819, weekly reset 2026-08-31T04:59:59Z (well past stop_at), gear 4, ratio 0.32, probe_ok true. Capacity is real; the run OPENS. Contrast run #7, whose kickoff probe wrote weekly_used_pct 100 fifteen minutes before 381 dead spawns.

PLAN independently reproduced cycle 0's D-R8-2 finding by a different route (.github/workflows/test.yml carries an explicit written refusal to add a count assertion), and raised a SECOND premise objection: S-5's 127-vs-129 gap is most likely CI depth-1 skips vs a local full clone, not staleness — both numbers true of different environments. Neither is accepted as fact; W-1 and W-5 exist to measure them, and both items now carry the counter-hypothesis in their notes so a builder cannot quietly assume the spec's framing.

The entire citation-window risk is concentrated in W-7, the only item touching test/ (inside the README citation pathspec). Closing that window needs a new Actions run id, requiring both a successful push and Actions API access — neither confirmed from this environment. W-7 is sequenced last among code-touching items, gated on a confirmed ability to obtain a run id, and must predict the window in its own commit message (S-8). Every other item lands in tools/, docs/ or REPORT.md, outside the pathspec. L-043's pathspec-guard clause applied at PLAN time rather than discovered at merge time.
